description:
Found while reviewing TRA-1690's pre-registered grading rule against the surface TRA-1689 actually shipped. Two defects in `cost-aware-gate-ledger.ts`, both in the observe-only path. Both would have silently voided the RV observe window, and neither is visible from the SHA.

`hydrateCostAwareGateFromDisk` sanitized the record kind as:

```

- `admitted` gains a phantom, and `avgAdmittedGrossR` is dragged toward 0.

- `absDelta` is dropped.

And it is not merely a misread: hydrate **compacts the file to the sanitized lines** (`kept.push(JSON.stringify(clean))`), so the first boot after a breach **overwrites the evidence on disk**. One-way. The observe ledger's whole promise is that it s

title: TRA-1647B: Add a per-structure entry-delta CEILING (0.55) — the cost gate is algebraically a floor and cannot cut the OTM loss tail
description:
The cost-aware gate is **algebraically a delta floor** and therefore structurally cannot cut the OTM loss tail. This is the code change the TRA-1647 re-grade needs. **Demo-only, observe-grade; no live-capital path** (same containment as TRA-1602 — `costAwareGateReject` early-returns on `mode !== 'demo'`).

I own the thresholds (TRA-1599); I do not write app code — hence the delegation. Numbers below are mine and are final.

## Why the gate can't do this itself

`modeledGrossR = min(mult·|Δ|, cap)·(rewardR + 1) − 1`, admit iff `modeledGrossR ≥ bar`. Solve:

> **admit ⟺ |Δ| ≥ (bar + 1) / (mult · (rewardR + 1))**

At the shipped default that is exactly **|Δ| ≥ 0.495**. It is a **one-sided floor**, and no value of `OPTION_COST_GATE_WIN_PROB_DELTA_MULT` / `_DEFAULT_REWARD_R` / `_WIN_PROB_CAP` / `_MIN_GROSS_R` changes that form — they only slide the floor. Raising delta always *increases* modeled R, so **a higher-delta contract is always more admissible**. The gate can never reject the top of the delta range.

The cost-aware fire bar ([TRA-1602](/TRA/issues/TRA-1602), armed demo `2160deb`) rests on a **spread-cross number that was never measured**. `option-cost-gate.ts` says so itself:

The shipped model is `commission 0.05R + spreadCross 1.00R + margin 0.20R => 1.25R bar`.

description:
Parent: TRA-1434 (QuantTrader trade review).

The book-level give-back cap (bookGiveBackDecision in packages/engine/src/exit-rules.ts, BOOK_GIVEBACK_CAP_PCT=0.40) halts NEW entries for the whole session once the book surrenders >40% of the day's peak (realized+open) gain. STEP 0 - confirm /api/health/version commit is a8d1fd7 or a descendant. If older, autoDeploy has not landed; note and exit.

  (a) uptimeSec ~85min AND rssBytes climbing toward/over ~1.5-1.9GB with small external/arrayBuffers => native RSS burst overshot the cgroup ceiling within one acute sample => arena cap insufficient; escalate to LOWERING watchdog rssMaxBytes for an earlier GRACEFUL self-restart

title: TRA-1463 watchdog trip-reason capture (bqb1 ~85min restart)
description:
Verify the TRA-1463 durable fix held on bqb1. Each run: GET https://tradingai-bqb1.onrender.com/api/health/watchdog and /api/health/version.

CONTEXT: the ~85min kill is an EXTERNAL kill (cgroup SIGKILL 137 acute RSS burst, or health-check SIGTERM after 5-6 consecutive 502s) that BYPASSES the watchdog's own exit path, so lastTrip stays null on reboot and cannot attribute it. a8d1fd7 (current fix, shipped 2026-07-08) adds a throttled last-known-alive breadcrumb written on a 15s timer to <DATA_DIR>/watchdog-liveness.json; on the next boot it is surfaced as watchdog.priorLiveness. cd62a40 (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2) remains in place to bound native RSS fragmentation.

STEP 0 - confirm /api/health/version commit is a8d1fd7 or a descendant. If older, autoDeploy has not landed; note and exit.

STEP 1 - read watchdog.priorLiveness. If NON-null, the prior instance was externally killed; attribute from its last breadcrumb:
  (a) uptimeSec ~85min AND rssBytes climbing toward/over ~1.5-1.9GB with small external/arrayBuffers => native RSS burst overshot the cgroup ceiling within one acute sample => arena cap insufficient; escalate to LOWERING watchdog rssMaxBytes for an earlier GRACEFUL self-restart

description:
## Follow-up to [TRA-1374](/TRA/issues/TRA-1374) — kill the burst, not just its symptom

The [TRA-1374](/TRA/issues/TRA-1374) acute RSS watchdog trip (shipped `3b13fe2`) converts the abrupt `nonZeroExit: 137` cgroup SIGKILLs into clean ~30s restarts, but the box still *cycles* every ~5-6 min because a heavy tick spikes RSS from steady ~0.3-0.75 GB past the 2 GB ceiling in under one metric-sample window. title: Fix: demo starting-equity edit / post-archive regen wipes today calendar P&L (TRA-1398 spinoff)
description:
**Bug (board-reported on TRA-1398):** updating the DEMO account starting equity after market close erased today's realized P&L from the P&L Calendar (Richard's demo book — today's cell → $0.00 while prior days survived).

**Root cause (diagnosed):** the equity edit is a red herring — it only rebased `totalEquity`. The eraser is a post-archive empty regeneration of today's report:
1. The 21:00 ET archive (`runDailyCloseForAllUsers`) writes today's report WITH trades, then `archiveClosedTrades()` empties `allClosedPositions` (`signal-engine.ts:9787`).
2. A later re-run of `generateAndSaveReport` for TODAY (a Render redeploy after 21:00 resets the in-memory `lastArchiveDate` guard in `scheduler.ts:361` and re-fires the close) regenerates the cell from the now-empty ledger -> `trades:[]`, `realizedPnl:0`, and overwrites the good file (`index.ts:936`). Prior days are frozen files -> survive.
- Confirmed live on bqb1: Richard `/api/reports/2026-07-06?mode=demo` -> trades:[], realizedPnl:0, totalEquity 2241.69 (vs ~$25.3k on Jul 1/2 — proving the regen ran after the equity edit).

**Fix (done, on a branch, tests green):** `fix/TRA-1398-calendar-clobber` (commit b4ff5c9).

title: bqb1 residual cycling: ~3-min health-check-timeout restarts (event-loop starvation) persist after the fan-out fix
description:
## bqb1 still cycles ~every 3 min after the fan-out fix — residual TRA-1374 cold-start storm (event-loop starvation), NOT 137

Discovered during the [TRA-1389](/TRA/issues/TRA-1389) soak of the [TRA-1387](/TRA/issues/TRA-1387) fan-out fix. Under commit **c76398a** (live since 2026-07-06 22:32Z):

- RSS is clean (~428 MB vs 1900 MB ceiling); **no `nonZeroExit:137`** under the fix. The native-memory burst is fixed.
- BUT the box restarts every ~3 min on `server_failed: unhealthy — HTTP health check failed (timed out after 5s)`:
  - 22:37:20, 22:40:59, 22:43:50 (each -> new process; watchdog `startedAt` matches the event to the second).
- This is the original **TRA-1374** root: crypto-feed cold-start storm starves the event loop >5s on each boot, so Render's 5s health probe times out and restarts -> self-perpetuating loop. Independent of RSS/137.

### Why this is a separate issue
TRA-1389 -> TRA-1387 -> TRA-1374 already forms a chain; TRA-1389 cannot block directly on its own descendant TRA-1374 (cycle). This carries the residual work so the soak has a first-class blocker.

title: Recalibrate options per-trade max-loss cap governor (2% + $500 floor)
description:
Delegated from TRA-1346 by QuantTrader. Risk-parameter decision is made; this is the code change.

**Problem:** Every AI options idea returns enterable:false. The pre-trade gate (packages/engine/src/options/multi-leg-gate.ts, DEFAULT_MAX_LOSS_PCT_CAP = 0.01) caps per-trade max loss at 1% of equity. On the $25,000 demo book that is $250, which is below the max loss of a single standard $5-wide defined-risk vertical (~$350-450/lot). Result: 100% of ideas blocked.

**Required change (governor):** per-trade max loss ceiling = max(0.02 * equity, min(500, 0.05 * equity)).
- Raise DEFAULT_MAX_LOSS_PCT_CAP from 0.01 to 0.02 (2%).
- Add an ABSOLUTE dollar floor of $500 to capUsd so small books can still enter one standard single lot, BUT clamp that floor so it never exceeds 5% of equity (protects tiny live books). Suggest new export DEFAULT_MAX_LOSS_ABS_FLOOR = 500 and DEFAULT_MAX_LOSS_FLOOR_EQUITY_FRAC = 0.05.
- In evaluateMultiLegPreTrade, compute capUsd = Math.max(equity * cap, Math.min(absFloor, equity * floorFrac)) instead of equity * cap.

**Files:**
- packages/engine/src/options/multi-leg-gate.ts (cap constant + capUsd formula + reason string)
- packages/server/src/options-account.ts

## Fix CryptoDCA so it actually accumulates/averages a held position (from [TRA-951](/TRA/issues/TRA-951))

description:

Design the desktop UX for the trade-proposal confirmation flow that LeadDev will build.

title: TRA-813 P2/3: Ratify auto-confirm thresholds & daily execution caps
description:
Parent: [TRA-813](/TRA/issues/TRA-813). From the board-approved [plan](/TRA/issues/TRA-813#document-plan).

## Ask
Ratify (confirm, adjust, or replace) the proposed auto-confirm rules and daily execution caps that gate AI-placed orders. LeadDev's execution wiring depends on the final numbers.

## Proposed defaults to ratify
- **Auto-confirm only when** `conviction >= 0.70` AND notional `<= $250` AND the per-mode kill switch is on.
- Everything else queues for manual board approval.
- Demo and live evaluated independently; **live never auto-confirms in v1** (manual-only).
- **Daily execution caps** (separate from the $2/day LLM spend cap): max **5** agent-placed live orders/user/day, max **$1,000** notional/user/day. Demo uncapped beyond the existing 2% sizing cap.

## Deliverable
A short ratified-thresholds note (comment or issue document) giving the final values + rationale. No code. Hand back here when done so LeadDev's build can consume the numbers.

- bear_call_spread: 76 trades, win 13%, exits = 63 time_stop / 8 stop_loss / 5 take_profit.
- debit_spread: 117 trades, win 19%, exits = 95 time_stop / 13 stop_loss / 9 take_profit.

Two impossibilities prove the bug:

title: TRA-920 A: Daily learning loop - digest shadow outcomes into adaptive signal weights
description:
Parent: [TRA-920](/TRA/issues/TRA-920). Blocked by [TRA-921](/TRA/issues/TRA-921) (needs the reversal-checklist shadow ledger as its input data).

This is the headline ask of TRA-920: agents that 'learn and get better each day'. Today the shadow ledgers RECORD outcomes but nothing feeds them back into signal generation. Build the feedback loop.

## Scope
- A post-market daily routine (use the routines system, model after TRA-849 briefing) that reads the day's shadow ledger rows, joins them to resolved outcomes, and folds them into a persisted per-symbol / per-pattern / per-checklist-score stats store (win%, avg realized R, false-signal rate, sample count).
- Derive learned multipliers from those stats (e.g. de-weight a pattern whose recent false-signal rate exceeds a threshold; up-weight checklist scores that historically resolve to target). Require a minimum sample size before a multiplier moves off neutral.
- Apply the multipliers as a SCORING input to future signals (not a hard gate at first) so behavior stays auditable and reversible.

description:
Parent: [TRA-920](/TRA/issues/TRA-920).

title: Scope non-operator users out of the shared Live broker (TRA-856 data leak)
description:
## Scope a non-operator user out of the shared Live broker (multi-tenant data leak)

Parent: [TRA-856](/TRA/issues/TRA-856) — *New account should not have open position already*. QA confirmed the leak and root cause there; this is the durable backend fix.

**Bug:** Any brand-new user who flips to Live sees the **operator's shared broker positions** (reproduced: 85 Coinbase holdings on a fresh crypto-Live account). Cause: the live-broker builders fall back to shared `process.env` creds for **every** user, not just the pinned operator.

**Fix:**

1. `crypto-engine.ts buildLiveBroker()` — only allow the `process.env.COINBASE_API_KEY/SECRET` fallback when the engine's owning user is the operator pin (`LIVE_EQUITY_BOOT_USER`, default `admin`, per `signal-engine.ts:5130`). Otherwise, if the user has no per-user crypto creds → return `null` (empty live dashboard). The crypto engine currently has **no username**; thread it in (mirror stocks' `setAlertUsername`, wired in `user-context.ts`).
2. `signal-engine.ts buildTradierLiveEquityClient()` — apply the same operator-scoping to its `TRADIER_API_TOKEN / TRADIER_ACCOUNT_ID` env fallback.
3. Per-user creds entered in Settings continue to work

title: P4 — Trading Agents gating mode: route APPROVE recommendations as orders (demo-first)
description:
## P4 — Trading Agents gating mode (route orders behind risk caps)

Let an APPROVE recommendation's `proposedSignal` actually trade. Today the advisory stub never routes (`signal-engine.ts:2497`); this wires the route.

### Scope
- Route `proposedSignal` through the **existing** order path so it inherits the deterministic `RiskManager` hard caps, halts, and the [TRA-526](/TRA/issues/TRA-526) kill switch — agents never bypass risk (TRA-529 §2B).
- **Demo-first (default):** gating routes in **demo mode only**. Live routing is a separate flag gated behind board approval + CTO sign-off.
- Idempotency / dedup so one recommendation cannot double-fire across ticks; position + exposure checks before submit.

### Acceptance
- In demo, an APPROVE recommendation places a **risk-checked** order.
- Kill switch + risk caps demonstrably override agent orders.
- **No live orders** until the separate go-live gate is cleared.

Blocked by [TRA-795](/TRA/issues/TRA-795). Parent: [TRA-794](/TRA/issues/TRA-794). Spec: TRA-529 P4.

title: Make per-trade R fee-aware in BacktestRunner (net expectancy series) — TRA-815 fix
description:
## Why
Code fix delegated from [TRA-815](/TRA/issues/TRA-815) (workstream A of [TRA-814](/TRA/issues/TRA-814)). QuantTrader has traced the root cause; this issue is the application-code change (shared `BacktestRunner` + types + regression test). QuantTrader owns the re-run/report afterwards.

## Root cause (confirmed)
The per-trade **R-multiple is fee-blind**. `tradeR()` in `packages/backtest/src/runner.ts:90-100` computes R purely from prices:

```
((exitPrice - entryPrice) * dir) / stopDistance   // no commission term
```

`computePnl()` (`runner.ts:248-260`) *does* net commission into dollar PnL, and `closed.pnl = optimisticPnl` is fee-inclusive — that is why `totalPnl`, `profitFactor`, `sharpeRatio`, `maxDrawdown` **do** differ by cost arm in the report. But `tradeRs` (`runner.ts:604`) and `expectancy` (`runner.ts:734`) never see fees. TRA-523 pools exactly `oosRes.tradeRs` (`run-tra523-fee-aware.ts:303`), so pooled expectancy / PF / bootstrap are byte-identical (-0.2056R) across all five cost arms. Evidence in the report itself: for any symbol (e.g. BTC-USD bb_fade) `oos.expectancyR` is identical across arms while `oos.profitFactor`/`sharpe`/`totalPnlUsd` differ.

## Required

Prerequisite for every go/no-go decision. That is impossible if fees were applied to the pooled metric. Our 'fee-aware' validation is **not actually fee-aware**, so every net-of-fees verdict from this tooling is untrustworthy.

## Scope
- Trace where `costArms` feed (or fail to feed) the pooled expectancy / profit-factor / bootstrap computation in the TRA-523 harness (`packages/backtest/src/run-tra523-fee-aware.ts` and the shared runner it calls).
- Make per-arm fees actually flow into per-trade PnL so expectancy/PF/bootstrap differ by arm.
- Add a regression test: a higher-fee arm must yield strictly lower net expectancy than `gross_0` for a fixture strategy with nonzero turnover.
- Re-run TRA-523 and commit the corrected per-arm table.

Cost arms produce monotonically worse net expectancy as fees rise; regression test green; corrected report committed and pushed to `main`.
